chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala, from al-Qasim ibn Burayd, from Ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), in

a man who set up a net in the water, then returned to his house and left it standing; he came to it later and found fish had fallen into it and died. He said: 'His hand did not act [directly], so there is no objection to eating what fell into it.'
ai.seo_question: Is fish caught in a stationary net considered halal if it dies in the water?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that fish caught in a stationary net left by a person are permissible because the net's action is considered an extension of the owner's hand, yet the fish dies from natural causes rather than direct slaughter. This ruling distinguishes between fish that die in water due to human intervention (which may be makruh or haram depending on the school) and those caught passively, reinforcing the principle of 'what the hand did not kill' in Shia fiqh. The hadith is cited in al-Isfabar under the chapter of prohibited floating fish, highlighting the nuance between death by drowning and death by capture.
